artworks.title: Eumaeus, Chief Swineherd
artworks.description: Polish history painter Jan Styka isolates Homer's swineherd as a monumental pastoral figure — staff, cloak, and the weathered face of the slave who never stopped waiting for Odysseus. The canvas treats Eumaeus not as a side character but as the Odyssey's type of loyalty below the palace.

artworks.title: Ulysses Attacked by the Dogs of Eumaeus
artworks.description: Illustration to Odyssey 14: the disguised Odysseus approaches the swineherd's steading and is set upon by Eumaeus' dogs before the loyal slave calls them off and offers hospitality. Schützenberger makes the hut's threshold the first true welcome home — Eumaeus' dogs almost spoil the recognition that will save Ithaca.

artworks.title: Odysseus and Telemachus in the Hut of Eumaeus
artworks.description: Genelli's outline composition for the Odyssey: Odysseus sits by the fire as Eumaeus discovers Telemachus at the hut's entrance — the reunion of father and son under the swineherd's roof (Book 16). Eumaeus is the hinge of the scene, the loyal host whose steading becomes the conspiracy's first safe room.

artworks.title: Slaughter of the Suitors (with Eumaeus)
artworks.description: Campanian red-figure bell-krater in the Louvre (CA 7124): Odysseus, Telemachus, and Eumaeus cut down the suitors in the hall — the swineherd armed beside his king at the climax of the Odyssey. Named among the killers on the vase, Eumaeus leaves the hut for the palace and finishes the loyalty Homer gave him.

artworks.title: Telemachus Recognizes Odysseus in the House of Eumaeus
artworks.description: Oil in the Weimar Schlossmuseum: Nahl stages the recognition of Odysseus by Telemachus inside the swineherd's house, with Eumaeus' steading as the setting Athena chooses for the plot's turning point. The painting keeps the humble hut — not the palace — as the place where the royal family first reunites.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: Konchalovsky's miniseries keeps the swineherd's hut as Odysseus' first loyal roof — Eumaeus as the slave who never stopped waiting.

popCulture.title: Eumaeus
popCulture.description: Eumaeus endures as the faithful swineherd — Homer's type of loyalty below the palace, who feeds the beggar who is his king.
